steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: understand the browser-to-Java boundary
steps.detail: A backend-for-frontend, or BFF, is the server-side adapter that lets a browser use its own site's session while communicating with the business APIs. It is not a replacement business backend. Read apps/customer-web-next/src/lib/server-api.ts. apiBaseUrl requires an HTTPS CRAVES_API_BASE_URL; authenticatedApiFetch obtains the access credential from the server cookie, validates the requested path, applies a timeout and disables response caching. For protected administrative requests it checks the actual Auth identity before forwarding. Follow apiTarget as well: Academy routing uses the gateway's /academy surface while ordinary APIs retain their existing base. Do not concatenate paths from memory or copy authentication tokens into browser storage to make a request work.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: constrain both the route and its response
steps.detail: A generic proxy accepting arbitrary destinations can accidentally expose internal services. Read academyRoute in academy-route-policy.ts: allowed methods, path segments and query parameters are explicit. Source indexes currently use a single digit, so a course with more than ten source entries would exceed this existing client contract. Query duplication, traversal and malformed plan revisions are rejected. On the response side, a TypeScript interface is only a compile-time description; it does not validate incoming JSON. Keep malformed upstream responses distinct from empty valid results. A temporary timeout should not produce a fabricated course list or clear a potentially valid administrator session without the established renewal logic.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: defend a constrained adapter
steps.detail: From apps/customer-web-next run node --test --experimental-strip-types src/lib/academy-route-policy.test.ts. Read every rejection case, including an encoded traversal, a wrong method, duplicated query fields and source index 10. Add a local negative test for an unknown query field using the existing test style. Trace one permitted catalog request from AcademyDashboard through its BFF route, server-api, apiTarget and Java controller. Write an expected response-state matrix for 200 valid JSON, 200 malformed JSON, denied access and temporary dependency failure. No test should obtain a live token or call a real protected endpoint. Deliver the route allowlist and an assertion that an unsupported destination cannot reach the network dependency.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a complete browser/BFF/gateway/Java sequence and a failing-then-passing negative route test. Explain why server cookies, runtime response validation and backend authorization remain necessary even when the UI hides a control.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: distinguish code, build, routing and acceptance
steps.detail: A Next.js build validates the configured application compilation and build-time checks; it does not prove a deployed domain serves that image or that an authenticated journey works. Identify the exact source SHA, image digest or build identifier, deployed Container App revision, traffic path, BFF configuration and backend contract. Academy uses the existing administrative web application, not a newly provisioned site. Course text delivered by the existing backend catalog can be expanded without changing unrelated customer pages. Before deciding to deploy the web application, inspect whether the actual renderer or client contract changed. Preserve approved payment/delivery configuration and one-replica limits rather than reusing a broad platform release for a text update.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: native mobile has additional release boundaries
steps.detail: React Native shares TypeScript concepts with the web but produces native Android/iOS applications. A JavaScript unit test, Metro development session, debug Android build, signed release build and store-distributed application are different artifacts. Read apps/mobile/package.json and the repository's existing scripts instead of assuming web commands apply to mobile. A Jest script named test:e2e does not by itself prove that a physical device or native payment handoff was exercised. Store accounts, signing keys and provisioning profiles belong in their approved consoles and secure build configuration, never in training files. Do not change native dependencies or app signing merely to complete an Academy lesson.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: build an evidence ladder for two clients
steps.detail: For web, record the commands npm ci, npm run typecheck and npm run build from apps/customer-web-next, with the lockfile and CI runtime versions actually used by the repository. For mobile, inspect npm scripts before choosing the focused Jest tests; distinguish them from npm run android or npm run ios, which require the native toolchain. Create a release worksheet with rows for unit tests, parser tests, build, deployment/install, authenticated navigation and payment deep-link recovery. Mark each executed or not executed with its exact artifact. Do not label a mocked payment journey as a real charge or an Android debug APK as an iOS/App Store release.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: separate web and native release ladders with honest test limits, configuration ownership and rollback points. No app store publication, signing change or production deployment occurs during this training exercise.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: follow a mobile response into safe state
steps.detail: Read apps/mobile/src/features/customerOrders/api/customerOrdersApi.ts beside customerOrdersApi.test.ts. The adapter validates the backend response and constructs the allowed client representation; it does not simply cast arbitrary JSON to an interface. The reviewed test proves that customer identity and private address phone/latitude data are not retained in the exposed order representation, that monetary values are normalized into the expected shape and that unknown order status or an oversized backend window is rejected. Trace the API adapter into its query/state consumer and then the screen. State ownership matters: server state, a navigation target and an unfinished form are not the same thing and should not be stored indiscriminately together.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: process restoration and payment handoff
steps.detail: A mobile operating system can terminate an application while the user is in a payment provider or another screen. Read sessionManager.ts and the navigation process-restoration tests to identify which metadata is retained and what must be revalidated. paymentRecovery.test.ts models success only after backend verification and checkout reconciliation agree. A provider handoff error is not automatically a failed payment when backend state says the payment succeeded. Conversely, returning to the app is not proof of payment. Never create a new provider order merely because the original screen was recreated, and never persist raw authentication credentials inside an arbitrary navigation payload.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: test restoration with synthetic data
steps.detail: From apps/mobile run npm test -- --runInBand --runTestsByPath src/features/customerOrders/customerOrdersApi.test.ts src/features/payment/paymentRecovery.test.ts. Inspect the mocked HTTP/provider dependencies first. Build scenarios for a normal order read, malformed response, unknown status, lost process state and a handoff error followed by a verified paid checkout. For each, state the safe visible screen and the backend read required before showing success. Add one local response-privacy or restoration fixture using the existing test pattern. Deliver the API-to-state-to-screen map and a list of fields that must never enter persistent client storage. Native device behavior remains untested unless separately exercised.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: parser/privacy tests and a recovery state table that distinguishes transport, provider handoff and authoritative payment state. The learner must explain why restoring a screen must not repeat a money movement.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: build one read-only feature in both clients
steps.detail: Training-only feature brief: display a concise order-history summary derived exclusively from the existing authorized order response. It may show already public fields such as status and item count; it must not introduce new business statuses, expose private pickup information or call a mutation on render. Begin with the actual backend DTO and existing client adapters. Write a single approved response contract and two client presentation plans: a Next.js component behind the constrained BFF and a React Native component using its established API/state layer. Share semantics, not unsafe assumptions that DOM and native navigation behave identically. Keep transactional rules in the Java owner.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: model every important user-visible state
steps.detail: Define loading, empty, populated, denied, offline/temporary failure and malformed-response states before drawing a card. Preserve the underlying list position and stable item identity when opening and closing details. Avoid a late asynchronous response restoring protected data after logout. Do not use a loading spinner forever for a terminal permission denial, or label a transport failure as no orders. Keep buttons disabled only for the action actually in flight and prevent accidental duplicate mutation requests when a read-only exercise is later extended. For accessibility, include keyboard focus and meaningful labels on the web and screen-reader labels/touch behavior on native; a CSS or unit-test check is not a full accessibility audit.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: implement and review the local client slice
steps.detail: Create training/order-summary-clients. Use synthetic responses to implement the smallest web and native summary components with their existing route/API adapters. Add runtime parser tests, one private-field rejection, an unknown status case and empty/error presentation assertions. Run the focused client tests and web typecheck/build; run native Jest without contacting production. Provide full file contents, the shared contract, two state tables and a rollback note. A reviewer should be able to trace every rendered value back to an allowed API field and prove no payment/order/delivery write is called. Do not publish a store build, change signing or deploy customer web as part of Academy publication.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: two local read-only client implementations, complete state handling and privacy/contract tests. A beautiful card without authorization, parsing, error handling and recovery is not a complete feature.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: choose tests nearest to the regression
steps.detail: Use pure tests for route policy and parsers, service tests for authoritative business rules, component tests for presentation decisions, and real browser/native acceptance for deployed interactions. Tie every result to an exact source revision. A full Next.js build can detect integration errors outside a focused test, while a successful native Jest run cannot prove signing or device deep links. Test ordinary customer sessions separately from administrator session renewal. Preserve answer/form state only inside the established secure lifecycle and clear protected state on genuine logout. A source-level reduced-motion rule or keyboard handler is evidence of implementation, not proof that every assistive technology path has been validated.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: fix the failing client boundary first
steps.detail: For a 400 or invalid-upstream-response error, capture the exact request path, allowed query shape, upstream status and parsed contract using redacted evidence. Verify which domain and application revision actually handled the request. Do not restart payment, delivery, subscription or notification services because a client parser rejected a response. For stale frontend assets or a deployment mismatch, use the existing client rollback and routing evidence. For a mobile incident, consider the installed app version and server compatibility because store updates are not instantly adopted by all users. Retain backward-compatible API responses and do not force users into repeated payments to work around navigation defects.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: conduct a web/mobile incident rehearsal
steps.detail: Create three synthetic incidents: an Academy source route exceeds its allowed index, an order parser encounters an unknown status, and a payment handoff returns after process restoration. For each, identify the first violated contract, expected UI, safe retry/read, forbidden side effect and smallest regression test. Run the actual route, order-adapter and payment-recovery tests. Prepare a deployment/install evidence sheet and mark all real browser/device checks not executed unless observed. Include a compatibility check for the prior client version and a narrow rollback target. No customer transaction, provider call, native signing change or unrelated backend deployment is required.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: three reproducible diagnoses, regression tests and client-specific recovery plans. The reviewer must distinguish a passing test suite from a verified authenticated browser or native-device journey.
